blocks.html: Proton Mining builds and operates bitcoin mining sites, and runs the machines it sells at every one of them. We are best known for running on power nobody else wants — landfill gas, flared gas, curtailed grid.
Buy and host miners, find a site for your own operation, or put your energy to work.

Every day, energy gets thrown away because there is no economic way to move it to a buyer. Gas gets flared at the wellhead. Landfill methane gets vented. Wind and solar get curtailed when the grid cannot take them. That energy has no price because it has no customer.
Bitcoin mining is the one industrial load that can show up wherever the energy already is, buy every kilowatt-hour at a price that works, and switch off the moment somebody needs it more.

Stranded energy on one side.
Hashrate on the other.
Flare gas, landfill gas, curtailed renewables, and behind-the-meter surplus. Real energy, priced at or below zero because nothing is there to consume it.
We bring generation, containers, and machines to the energy, instead of waiting years for transmission to bring the energy to a market.
Mining is fully interruptible. We curtail in seconds when the grid calls, when prices spike, or when a host needs the power back — no process to restart, nothing spoiled.
Choose your next step.
Buy and host miners with Proton, ask us to find a potential site for your own operation, or explore a partnership around your energy.
You own the machines. We provide the power, the racks, the cooling, the network, and the hands — and you keep every satoshi they earn.
You have gas you are flaring, methane you are venting, or power you cannot sell. We finance, build, and run the load that buys it — on your land, on your terms.

We screen candidate sites against our own database of flare volumes, landfill gas capture, industrial facilities, and environmental permit records before anyone drives out to look at one. Power availability, gas duration, land control, interconnect distance, and jurisdiction all get scored up front — so the sites that reach diligence are the ones that can actually be built.

Metered gas composition and volume over time, or a real load study behind the meter. We model each site across a full range of hashprice and energy-cost scenarios, not a single optimistic case. If a site only works at one bitcoin price, we do not build it.

Generation, switchgear, transformers, containers, and network go in as one package. Pads, permits, and interconnection are handled before hardware ships. Machines are racked, mapped, and pointed at your pool before a site is called live.

Monitored around the clock from our own operations software — per-machine hashrate, temperature, power draw, and payouts, reconciled daily. Curtailment is automated against price and grid signals. You get the same numbers we do, every month, in a statement you can audit.

For Proton-hosted projects, we source the energy, coordinate the build and operate the fleet. For your own mining or hosting operation, our separate energy site sourcing service helps assess potential locations, existing infrastructure and remaining capital.
Energy-first site sourcing. We built our own screening stack over flare, landfill, facility, and permit data. Site selection is a data problem before it is a real-estate problem.
One counterparty, whole stack. Power procurement, construction, machine deployment, and daily operations sit with one team. Nobody gets handed off when something breaks.
Reporting you can check. Per-machine telemetry, pool payouts, and energy invoices reconciled monthly. If our statement and your pool dashboard disagree, we go find out why.
Curtailment is a feature. Our load is designed to disappear on command — which is exactly what makes us a welcome neighbour on a constrained grid or an active wellsite.
Whether you need miners and hosting, a potential energy site for your own operation, or a buyer for your gas or power, start with your requirements.

If you are flaring landfill gas, flaring associated gas, or curtailing generation because there is nowhere to send it, you have a product with no customer. We finance, build, and run the load that turns it into revenue — on your land, without a pipeline, and without you spending a dollar of capital.
Interruptible by design. If you need the gas or the power back, we shut down — on your schedule, not ours.
Four kinds of energy we can put to work.
All of them share one problem: production and demand are in the wrong place, or at the wrong time.

Municipal landfills, wastewater plants, and agricultural digesters with collected gas going to a flare because RNG upgrading does not pencil at your volume. We take gas that is currently destroyed for free and pay for it instead.

Oil producers with gas they cannot economically gather. Takeaway is constrained, the pipeline is years away, or the volume never justified the tie-in. We bring generation to the pad and consume the gas at the wellhead — cutting flare volume while turning a disposal cost into a revenue line.

Wind and solar assets that get dispatched down, hit negative pricing, or sit behind a congested interconnect. We become the buyer of last resort at the busbar — and we get out of the way instantly when the grid wants the power back.

Industrial sites with contracted capacity they are not using, self-generation running below load, or waste heat and pressure with no offtake. We soak up the margin between what you pay for and what you consume.
We bring the capital and the complexity.
Most partners want the revenue without inheriting a new line of business. That is exactly how we structure it.
All of the capital. Generation, switchgear, containers, machines, and site work are funded by us. Your capital budget is untouched.
Permitting and compliance. Air permits, noise, setbacks, and interconnect paperwork handled by our team, in your jurisdiction.
Build and commissioning. Pads, foundations, gas conditioning, and electrical, delivered as one contract with one accountable party.
Operations, forever. Staffed and monitored 24/7. Engine maintenance, machine repair, and curtailment response are ours, not yours.
Decommissioning. Bonded removal and site restoration at end of term, written into the agreement up front.
The energy. Gas volume and composition over time, or available electrical capacity with a real load profile behind it.
Site control. Surface rights or a lease you can assign, clean enough to survive diligence.
A decision maker. Someone who can sign a term sheet without a six-month committee cycle.
Pick the risk profile you want. Fixed and predictable, or tied to the upside — we will quote any of them on the same site.

We buy your gas at a fixed [$X.XX]/MMBtu, or your power at [$0.0XX]/kWh, on a take-or-pay style contract. Simple, bankable, and it moves the bitcoin price risk off your side of the table. What it does not do is remove that risk from the deal: a fixed price is only as good as the company paying it, so ask what stands behind the obligation before you weigh it against a share.

You supply the energy, we supply everything else, and mining revenue splits [XX]/[XX] after agreed operating costs. Lower floor than a fixed contract, meaningfully higher ceiling. Reporting is open-book, with the same telemetry we run on.

You lease us the pad and the interconnect for [$X,XXX] per month and take a [X]% royalty on gross production. Most common where the landowner is not the energy owner, or where a municipality needs a clean, predictable line item.
If your site is close on most of these, send it anyway — the edges are negotiable and we would rather look than guess.

You send volumes, composition, location, and land status. We run it through our screening model and come back with a yes, a no, or the two specific things that would turn a no into a yes. We do not sit on sites.
Non-binding terms covering structure, price, term, interruption rights, and pad requirements. Signed under NDA, with enough detail that neither side is surprised later.

Site walk, metered gas sampling, title and surface review, permit path confirmation, and a full economic model across hashprice scenarios. This is where a site either earns the build or gets returned to you with our reasoning.

Pad, foundations, gas conditioning, generation, switchgear, containers, and network. Long-lead equipment is ordered at term-sheet signing, not at the end of diligence, which is how the schedule holds.
Commissioning, then continuous operation with 24/7 monitoring. You get production reporting on the same cadence as your payments, and a direct line to the people actually running the site.
This is not a marketing claim about being green. It is a straightforward comparison against what happens to the gas today.
You do not need a data room. Volumes, a location, and who controls the land is enough for us to tell you whether it is worth either side’s time.

Buy the machines
and the place to run them.
Every machine we can source
You do not have to arrive with a container of miners. Pick what you want below, set the quantities, and we will source it — and host it on the same agreement if you want us to.

Specifications are the manufacturer’s. Prices are indicative as of — and are confirmed on quote — we source per order rather than holding stock, so the number that matters is the one on your quote, not the one on this page.
Enter it and the last two columns fill in. Nothing is assumed on your behalf — power is what decides which machine is best, and it is the one figure only you know.

Revenue is gross mining revenue at today’s network difficulty, before power, pool fees, downtime and any hosting cost. Difficulty has risen in most years, so a payback calculated at today’s is the optimistic end of the range rather than a forecast.

Sorted by efficiency, best first — joules per terahash decides what a machine costs to run. It is not the same question as which is the best buy: payback is, because it is the only column that weighs the purchase price against what the machine earns. A cheap machine with mediocre efficiency often pays for itself first.
Send it as a quote request
This opens a pre-filled draft in your own mail app — nothing is sent until you send it yourself. If nothing opens, copy the order and write to hosting@protonminingco.com.

This is the projection engine we use internally, put on the public site unchanged. Start from a fleet you are thinking of buying, or from energy you already have and want to put to work. Every assumption below is yours to change.
Specs fill in from the model you pick, and stay editable — an underclocked machine is a different machine. We can source any of them.
What this does and does not tell you.

Every figure here comes from assumptions you typed. Bitcoin price and network difficulty are the two that matter most and the two nobody can forecast. Move them and watch how fast the answer changes — that sensitivity is the most useful thing on this page.

No curtailment, no seasonal derate, no shipping, customs, or import duty, no insurance, and no bad luck. Pool variance is averaged away. Machines are assumed to run at the specs you entered for their whole life.

The single input with the most leverage is your power cost. That is the number we exist to change, by building on energy that is currently being flared, vented, or curtailed. Put a real quote in and see what it does.
What this models that most calculators do not.

Most bitcoin mining calculators answer one question: at
        today—s price and today—s difficulty, what does this machine earn per day? That number
        is true for about a fortnight. These are the things that decide whether a machine pays
        for itself, and they are the ones usually left out.

The comparison nobody runs. It plots what a fleet does against putting the same
            money into bitcoin on day one and holding it, and tells you which period the two
            cross over in — if they do. Both sides are figured after tax, which matters,
            because mined coins are income when they are mined and held coins are not.

Your share of the network shrinks every time somebody else plugs in, whether or not
            you do anything. Most models leave this at zero, which quietly assumes the network
            stops growing. Set it to what you actually believe, including negative — network
            difficulty fell about 15% over the first eight months of 2026.

The block subsidy is stepped down on projected halving dates rather than held flat,
            out to 2100. Over any horizon longer than about three years that is the difference
            between a projection and a straight line.

Hardware has a lifespan, a salvage value, and a date it stops being economic that
            arrives before the date it breaks. You can set all three, choose whether retired
            machines are replaced, and choose whether the proceeds are reinvested or taken out.

Mining income and capital gains are different taxes at different rates on different
            events. They are modelled as two figures rather than one blended number, because the
            comparison against simply holding bitcoin is meaningless if only one side is taxed.

If you have gas rather than hardware, start from the gas. Enter volume in mcf per
            day with your own heat rate and BTU content, and it works out the load that supports
            and the fleet that fills it. That is the question a flare owner actually has, and it
            is the reverse of the one every other calculator answers.

Pool fee, uptime, infrastructure cost, scheduled additions and
        an existing bitcoin treasury are all inputs too. Nothing is assumed on your behalf, and
        the scenario travels in the address bar — the URL is the whole state, so you can send
        it to somebody and they will see exactly what you saw.
